charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Nufarm Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Nufarm Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Nufarm Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Nufarm Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Nufarm Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Nufarm Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Nufarm Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Nufarm Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by segment
segmentRevenue.content:
Nufarm reports two divisions: Crop Protection, split into three regions (APAC, Europe, North America), and Seed Technologies (Hybrid Seeds, Bioenergy and Omega-3). A Corporate/unallocated line (not charted here) is immaterial to revenue.

For Nufarm Limited: the regions move on different cycles -- APAC on local weather and Australian dry conditions, North America on generic crop-chemical pricing competition, Europe on EU pesticide regulation -- while Seed Technologies has been under strategic review since FY2025 after an Omega-3 fish-oil price collapse and a Hybrid Seeds pullback from the Russia/Ukraine-affected European sunflower business.

What to watch:

  • Whether Crop Protection's regional mix is shifting toward or away from APAC, the FY2025 profit driver
  • Seed Technologies revenue stabilising or continuing to shrink post-review
  • FY2021-FY2024 figures are restated for the FY2025 reporting-segment change (seed treatment moved from Seed Technologies into the Crop Protection regions)

segmentMargin.title: Segment underlying EBITDA margin
segmentMargin.content:
Segment underlying EBITDA as a percentage of that segment's own revenue -- the profitability each region/division earns, before significant items.

For Nufarm Limited: management's FY2025 letter credits APAC with "record profitability" and an 18% increase in crop protection profit, while North America and Europe were streamlined and Seed Technologies absorbed most of the year's write-downs -- so a widening gap between APAC's margin and the other lines is the segment story, not a one-off.

What to watch:

  • APAC margin holding up versus North America/Europe margin recovery from the FY25 restructuring
  • Seed Technologies margin volatility around Omega-3 commodity prices
  • A segment's EBITDA briefly exceeding revenue-derived 100% would signal a reclassified material item, not genuine margin

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Nufarm Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Nufarm Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
